disposition: caffeine balanced across cycling formulations
assessment: The authors added caffeine to the placebo to approximate the amount in the tea catechin and ornithine formulation. Coffee was not assigned or compared.

disposition: combined extract and amino acid compared during exercise
assessment: The healthy crossover found lower effort ratings in fixed-load cycling after tea catechins and ornithine. Effort in the separate performance test was inconclusive. The study administered a mixture and did not enroll people with Parkinson disease.

disposition: separate prior cherry juice study
assessment: A prior cherry juice sleep study informed the washout duration. The tested drink contained green tea and chicory extracts, and the fatigue inventory's motivation subscale is distinct from Parkinson apathy.

disposition: separate prior cherry juice study
assessment: A cited tart cherry juice study informed washout duration. Neither arm in the current fatigue comparison was a cherry intervention.

disposition: background caffeine and whole supplement fatigue comparison
assessment: The Methods compare a proprietary tea and chicory supplement with placebo. Discussion mentions caffeine consumption among habits affecting sleep. No brewed coffee was assigned.

disposition: combined supplement and individual fatigue subscales
assessment: A ten-participant insomnia crossover compared the whole supplement with placebo. Physical fatigue favored the supplement while general fatigue was inconclusive. Its extract preparation, multi-ingredient comparison and study population leave the frozen claim unresolved.

disposition: canine olfactory comparison and location name
assessment: Maize oil was part of a detection-dog diet and the outcomes were scent detection. The text mentions Tinton Falls as an address. It gives no estimate of fall risk.

disposition: coffee was restricted in both crossover periods
assessment: Participants avoided other caffeinated and theanine-rich drinks including coffee. The assigned contrast was between two green tea formulations.

disposition: brewed tea formulation comparison in healthy adults
assessment: Low-caffeine tea showed lower Monday accumulated fatigue than standard tea. The Friday test was inconclusive. Both conditions included brewed tea and the components differed beyond caffeine.

disposition: caffeine restriction during athlete testing
assessment: Participants were asked to avoid caffeine before both cycling tests. The randomized exposure was encapsulated green tea extract compared with placebo.

disposition: capsule extract and muscle fatigability
assessment: The study measured exercise-induced electrical muscle activity in supplemented athletes. It did not compare brewed tea or measure Parkinson fatigue.

disposition: encapsulated caffeine with coffee intake questionnaire
assessment: The trial administered isolated caffeine and recorded usual tea and coffee frequency. It reports no overall condition effect on the measured mood outcomes and gives no brewed coffee comparison.

disposition: oregano was an odor identification stimulus
assessment: Oregano was presented in a concealed bottle during the smell task. The anxiety score concerned randomized caffeine administration and no fresh oregano was eaten.

disposition: thyme was an odor identification stimulus
assessment: Thyme was presented in a concealed bottle during the smell task. The mood comparison was assigned caffeine versus placebo, with no culinary thyme exposure.

disposition: cinnamon was an odor identification stimulus
assessment: Cinnamon was one of 15 odorants shown to participants under the same task procedure. The study did not assign cinnamon consumption to measure fatigue.

disposition: cinnamon was an odor identification stimulus
assessment: All participants performed an odor task including cinnamon. Tension or anxiety was compared by encapsulated caffeine assignment, with no randomized cinnamon contrast.

disposition: caraway was an odor identification stimulus
assessment: Caraway was presented as an odor sample. Fatigue was a questionnaire factor used in the caffeine experiment. The study supplies no effect of eating caraway.

disposition: nutmeg was an odor identification stimulus
assessment: The study exposed participants to nutmeg odor during identification testing and explicitly omitted the depression factor from its shortened mood questionnaire.

disposition: nutmeg was an odor identification stimulus
assessment: Nutmeg was presented as an odor sample and fatigue was a questionnaire factor. No ground nutmeg ingestion or effect estimate was tested.

disposition: corn oil comparator and baseline Geriatric Depression Scale
assessment: The corn oil and maltodextrin comparator was compared with a fish oil and whey supplement. The Geriatric Depression Scale appears in the baseline table without a reported post-assignment depression comparison.

disposition: corn oil comparator and fall risk context
assessment: The older-adult trial compared combination supplements and discussed baseline mobility and falls. Its reported performance measures do not provide a between-arm fall count.

disposition: coffee excluded from postoperative feeding protocol
assessment: Coffee appears in background research and on the list of excluded drinks. The daily fatigue result compares brewed tea with water.

disposition: brewed tea compared with water after gastric surgery
assessment: The report gives 77 analyzed and lower postoperative fatigue on days 3 to 6 under the randomized open-label brewed tea comparison. It measures short-term postoperative fatigue.
